claims.text: 48-year-old woman with ASD repair at age eight developed acute chest pain and orthopnoea 40 years later. CTPA excluded pulmonary embolism; CTCA identified a calcified 21×10×12 mm proximal ascending-aortic pseudoaneurysm with thrombus, flow and a thin inferior wall near the RCA ostium. Emergency redo surgery excised the sac and patched the 1 cm aortic defect with Gelweave. TOE showed good ventricular/valve function; recovery was uneventful, discharge on day seven included a three-month warfarin prescription targeting INR 2.5–3.5, and five-month follow-up was symptom-free.
